app_purpose: web application framework (Python); is_safe_url() guards the login/logout ?next= redirect
run_mode_notes: REAL published Django release installed per profile via pip (Django==1.7.5/1.8.0/1.8.18 on python:2.7-slim), booting a REAL Django project (app/ = manage.py + proj/{settings,urls,wsgi}.py) served by gunicorn (a real production WSGI server that forwards headers verbatim, confirmed by a direct WSGI call). The open redirect is triggered EXTERNALLY over HTTP: GET /login?next=<vector> (Host: app.local) hits the real `go` view, which calls Django's OWN django.utils.http.is_safe_url(next, host=request.get_host()) and returns a real 302. NO Django source is copied into a harness (the prior source-lift build was removed). The oracle observes the Location header of the real HTTP response, and the per-run FLAG (attacker redirect-host label) appears in that Location iff the installed Django's is_safe_url APPROVED the attacker-controlled next value -- so the flag-differential is driven exactly by the patched sink's decision.
faithfulness_nuance: Real Django (all three versions) applies django.core.handlers.base.fix_location_header, which absolutizes a RELATIVE Location via build_absolute_uri. This affects the two vectors differently: (a) the CVE-2017-7233 RESIDUAL http://app.local\@<FLAG>.evil.example is already absolute, so it is emitted verbatim as a GENUINELY EXTERNAL redirect on V1 (a browser resolves the authority as userinfo `app.local\` + host <FLAG>.evil.example -> off-origin); this is the benchmark's actual test target and is fully faithful. (b) The CVE-2015-2317 SEED \x7f//<FLAG>.evil.example is inherently RELATIVE (the leading control char is precisely what makes is_safe_url see netloc=='' and approve it), so fix_location_header absolutizes it to http://app.local/%7F//<FLAG>.evil.example -- the FLAG surfaces in the PATH, same-origin at the wire. This is unavoidable: any leading control char defeats scheme-relative parsing, so no control-char seed can survive absolutization as an external host. The seed's role in the gate is only (i) prove the vulnerable V0 approves the attacker input (FLAG present in Location) and (ii) be blocked by the CVE-2015-2317 control-char check on V1 (FLAG absent); both hold, and the V0-vs-V1 flag differential is cleanly driven by that control-char check. Observed as the honest behavior of REAL Django over REAL HTTP.
sink: django/utils/http.py :: is_safe_url(url, host) -- the installed Django package's own validator, invoked by the app's /login redirect view (mirrors django.contrib.auth.views.login's redirect_to gate)

faithful_core.notes: Runs the REAL Django release at each version; is_safe_url is exercised straight out of the installed django package over external HTTP. No source lifted.
faithful_core.control_char_choice: The original vector uses \x7f (DEL): unicodedata category 'Cc', rejected by exactly the CVE-2015-2317 fix (`if unicodedata.category(url[0])[0]=='C': return False`). Sent %7F-encoded; Django urldecodes it back to \x7f before is_safe_url().

v0.ref: pip Django==1.7.5; pre CVE-2015-2317: is_safe_url has NO control-char check

v1.ref: pip Django==1.8.0; CVE-2015-2317 fix present, CVE-2017-7233 still open

flag.resource: the login redirect target (Location header) approved by is_safe_url(next, host)
flag.placement: redirect-canary: per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is used as the attacker redirect-host label (next=%7F//<FLAG>.evil.example or http://app.local\@<FLAG>.evil.example); FLAG appears in the real 302 Location iff the installed Django's is_safe_url approves an off-origin redirect. Blocked -> 302 Location:/ (no FLAG). Nothing planted in app code.
flag.detect: flag token substring in the Location header of the real HTTP probe result

given_to_method: docker-compose.yml + Dockerfile (real Django install recipe, profile v1 = target)

evidence.fix_reference: pip Django==1.8.0; CVE-2015-2317 fix present, CVE-2017-7233 still open; pip Django==1.8.18; CVE-2017-7233 fix (double-validate raw+normalised)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: is_safe_url() was hardened repeatedly: CVE-2015-2317 added a leading-control-character check; CVE-2017-7233 (Django 1.8.18/1.10.7/1.11) fixed it to validate both the raw and backslash-normalised URL, closing basic-auth/backslash open-redirect vectors (e.g. http://otherserver\@example.com) still accepted by the 2015 fix.

provenance.notes: REAL Django releases installed via pip (1.7.5/1.8.0/1.8.18) on python:2.7-slim, real Django project served by gunicorn, open redirect triggered over external HTTP against the app's own /login redirect view (which calls Django's own is_safe_url). NO source-lift. Gate passed on real Docker (see repro.log). V0/V1/V2 is_safe_url behavior differs live: V0 approves the leading-control-char vector; V1 blocks it (control-char check) but approves the \@ basic-auth residual; V2 blocks both (double-validates raw+normalised).
